chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) is obligatory after every obligatory or voluntary prayer during the days of Tashriq.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah).
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greatest), specifically referring to the post-prayer supplications.
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٍ: Obligatory (referring to the five daily prayers).
key_terms.وَاجِبٌ: Obligatory; a legal ruling indicating a mandatory act in Shia jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Takbir after prayers during the days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: This narration from al-istibsar confirms the obligatory nature of reciting the Takbir after every prayer, both obligatory and voluntary, during the days of Tashriq. While often associated with the Eid al-Adha sacrifice, this ruling specifically applies to pilgrims in Mecca, highlighting the distinct jurisprudential status of the Hajj rituals within Shia fiqh. The emphasis on 'every prayer' underscores the continuous commemoration of God's greatness throughout these three days.
